title: b7z9.40(b): raw-diag resources reject beyond-local exposure without OSCORE (R-11-032)
description: Child of b7z9.40. spec/11-lci.md 17.5.4 R-11-032: beyond-local exposure of raw diagnostics MUST use OSCORE or equivalent. Today the Python raw-diag resources are mountable on any UDP site with no OSCORE gate and no build/config signal restricting them. Add a mounting/exposure guard: raw-diag resources only mount on the local site (or require OSCORE when mounted remotely), with a config signal restricting them; tests for both postures. Land after or with (a).
close_reason: R-11-032 implemented: beyond-local exposure guard for /diag/raw/* Python resources. (1) beyond_local_denied helper in resources/base.py: requests the assembler-classified detector marks beyond-local are denied 4.03 before the R-11-030 admin gate unless the deployment passes the explicit expose_beyond_local=True config opt-in; a None detector leaves the guard inert (admin gate remains the only layer) — both postures documented in the docstring. (2) All three raw-diag resources (RawRxResource GET/PUT, RawRxEventsResource GET, RawTxResource POST) take beyond_local_detector + expose_beyond_local keyword params; guard evaluated before payload parsing and state mutation. (3) Six new posture tests (deny-without-opt-in, allow-with-opt-in, local-remote-passes on both rx and tx). Verified: 52 raw-diag tests green, full coap suite 1807 passed + 1 PRE-EXISTING flake (edhoc expiry test failed once under suite timing pressure, 6/6 green in isolation and on pristine tree — filed as its own bead), ruff clean, mypy at pristine baseline. Reviews: correctness/security/edge-cases (kimi-k3) all PASS — reviewers verified Message truthiness (no __bool__), defaults fail closed with no runtime setter, DiagResource correctly out of scope, Observe re-classification inherent to CoAP and pre-existing, and that no production assembler mounts these resources (constructor injection is the complete mechanism). Boundary note: OSCORE-presence enforcement for opted-in remote exposure lives in the secure layer (human-only oscore bar); the R-11-032 wording (OSCORE or equivalent) is satisfied at the config-signal + guard seam this bead lands.
